resources.string: Add a Shadowsocks test server by entering its details or pasting an ss:// link. It then appears in Locations as a development location.
Servers are stored only on this device. Keys are encrypted with a key held in the Android Keystore.
You are connected. Changes take effect the next time you connect.
Optional · defaults to the server address
Its settings and key are removed from this device.
ss:// links do not say whether the server relays UDP, so it starts off. Turn it on only if your server allows UDP.
The link is missing the server address, port, cipher or key.
The link has no valid port (1–65535).
This server could not be loaded.
Paste an ss:// link to fill in the fields
The server\'s pre-shared key: 16 bytes, base64-encoded
Exactly as in your server configuration
Recommended. Shadowsocks 2022 with replay protection; uses a base64 key.
Older Shadowsocks AEAD cipher used by many existing servers; uses a password. Prefer a 2022 cipher when your server supports it.
The password contains a line break or other control character. Check that it was copied correctly.
Relay UDP (calls, games, DNS) through the server. Turn on only if your server allows UDP. When off, UDP is blocked and DNS is resolved by the server over TCP.
The key is stored encrypted with a key held in the Android Keystore and is never logged.
Changes apply the next time you connect.
Enter a valid host name or IP address.
The key must decode to exactly 16 bytes for 2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm.

Debug build only. Configure internal test servers.
Development build only. Test servers entered here are stored encrypted on this device, appear in Locations as development locations, and do not exist in release builds.
